text:
The news on Zach Hyman this week is his health. He left the Nov. 21 loss in Carolina after 8.8 minutes with a migraine, per Sportsnet, and did not play the next night in St. Louis. It's the second early exit of his season: he played 8.4 minutes against Detroit on Oct. 26 and didn't return until Nov. 7.

When he has played, it's been a slow year by his standard. He has 4 goals and 6 points in 14 games, and at 5v5 the Oilers have 45.1% of the expected goals with him on the ice. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him in the 98th percentile of forwards for driving his team's chances.

The finishing isn't the problem: 4 goals on 4.9 expected is about normal. The chances are thinner, 1.21 expected goals per 60 on his own shots against 1.82 last season, and his ice time over the last ten games is down almost four minutes from his usual.

Our talent range still puts his scoring rate near 2.36 points per 60, well above the 1.49 he's at. At 34, the open question is how much of his net-front game returns once he's healthy.
